note: Agents add findings here in proposed state. Every finding needs an annotated mobile-viewport screenshot (about 393x852) from the Vercel preview and a link to official documentation with the supporting line quoted. Without both, it shows Incomplete and is not eligible for approval. The owner has findings reviewed externally, then moves them to approved or rejected. Basis marks what was checked directly (verified) versus reported (belief).

findings.title: A sideways swipe anywhere on a detail screen pops it, mid-scroll

evidence.text: gestureEnabled: true, fullScreenGestureEnabled: true on court, run, player, notifications, match, challenge, settings and localplus.
Installed react-native-screens 4.16.0 honours the prop on iOS 26: line 79 disables the native recognizer, line 1254 returns topScreen.fullScreenSwipeEnabled.
Web cannot simulate the iOS back gesture (native UIKit only), so this marks the zone the code enables. It is a zone diagram, not a reproduction.

Issue reports stuck scroll inertia with the prop on, not a pop; the pop comes from the prop's documented behaviour. PR 3173 (Sep 2025) makes the full-screen swipe the native default on iOS 26 and ignores the prop in newer versions, so behaviour changes after a dependency bump (open Dependabot PR #69).
Quality, docs and Vercel build green. Expo Go preview publish was still running at 17:37 UTC. PR #72 holds the same fix, open since Oct 15, never merged.

findings.cause: The app opts into a full-width pan on every detail screen; the documented default is off.

fix.summary: Turn the full-screen gesture off (PR #80, same change as open PR #72, which was never merged). Risk is low: the edge swipe and back icon still work.

findings.risk: Low. Back by edge swipe and by the back icon are unchanged.
findings.verify: On a phone in the PR's Expo Go preview: the edge swipe goes back; a mid-screen sideways swipe on the court page does not. Belief until then.

screenshots.caption: Red zones: left edge strip is the iOS standard; the big box is what the code enables

docs.label: React Navigation Native Stack: fullScreenGestureEnabled
docs.quote: Whether the gesture to dismiss should work on the whole screen. ... Defaults to false.

findings.title: Form drawers drag from anywhere inside, then snap back

evidence.text: Did not set enableContentPanningGesture, whose default is true.
FormSheet drawers hold a plain ScrollView; the Log game form has its own scroll view.

evidence.ref: Web gesture test, Log game drawer, 393x852, mouse drag 200px inside the form
evidence.text: main: drawer top moved 183px down mid-drag and returned on release. With the fix it moved 0px. Grabber drag still moves it on both builds. A mouse stands in for touch.
Quality, docs and Vercel build green. The Vercel preview stops at sign-in, so the drawer proof is this test on a build of the same code.

findings.cause: Content panning is on for forms that should only move by the grabber.

fix.summary: New contentPanning prop on AppBottomSheetModal; form drawers pass false so only the grabber row drags. Scrolling and dynamic drawers are unchanged.

findings.risk: Low. Form drawers dismiss by grabber drag, tap-out or swipe down from the grabber only.
findings.verify: On a phone: open Log game, drag from inside the form (should not move), then drag the grabber (should move). Belief until then.

screenshots.caption: main: drawer dragged down from inside the form

docs.label: gorhom Bottom Sheet props: enableContentPanningGesture
docs.quote: Enable content panning gesture interaction. (default true; enableHandlePanningGesture default true)

findings.title: Schedule heatmap cells are under Apple's minimum touch size

evidence.text: smallTarget count 105 vs baseline 58; the 105 cells are about 41x25pt.
105 cells outlined in red on the Schedule screen.

screenshots.caption: 105 heatmap cells (red) are about 41x25pt; Apple: 44x44 default, 28x28 minimum

docs.label: Apple HIG: Accessibility
docs.quote: iOS default control size 44x44 pt; minimum 28x28 pt.

findings.cause: Dense by design (7 columns x 15 rows on one screen). Height 25pt is below even the 28pt minimum.

fix.summary: Needs your call on cell height or a row count change. hitSlop would make neighbouring cells overlap, so it is not proposed.

findings.risk: Visible layout change on the Schedule screen.
findings.verify: Re-run visual-qa after the decision; smallTarget should return to baseline.

18 text runs on the Schedule screen.

findings.cause: Small eyebrow and caption sizes accumulated across screens.

fix.summary: Raise to 11. A parked local change did: it cut off the court name at 375px until the On court label spacing was tightened (qa:visual 8 failures, then 0). Not yet a PR.

findings.risk: Visible design change across screens; needs your sign-off.
findings.verify: qa:visual at 3 phone sizes plus before/after mobile screenshots in the PR.

findings.title: Website says foreground-only location; the app uses Always

evidence.ref: Live privacy policy (desktop screenshot, not a mobile viewport)

evidence.text: The app requests Always location and background mode for auto check-in.

findings.cause: The policy and support page were written before background auto check-in. App Review compares the policy with the binary.

fix.summary: Change the website text to say location is used in the background for auto check-in. The site is not in the Expo repo.

findings.risk: Submission blocker if left as is.
findings.verify: Open the live privacy and support pages and read the location wording against app.json.
